page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 192 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 96 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 1536.0 GB of RAM, establishing a consistent memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU without discrete GPU acceleration.

Integrated hardware includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage for data operations requiring direct, low-latency disk access. The system provides a baseline networking speed of 300 Gbps. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Combining high-frequency processing cores, expansive memory density, and substantial local NVMe storage allows significant operational throughput and single-node resource consolidation. The architecture is configured for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise in-memory databases, distributed cache systems, big data processing pipelines, and high-throughput transactional database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and Intel x86_64 processors. It provides 192 vCPUs across 96 dedicated physical cores at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency, with simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. System memory comprises 1536.0 GB, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, without discrete GPU acceleration. Local storage is provisioned via 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD instance store capacity, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. By combining high-frequency processing cores, substantial memory capacity, and large local solid-state drives, the configuration offers high resource consolidation. This profile is engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory databases, real-time distributed analytics, high-throughput caching tiers, and large-scale transactional database management systems demanding rapid local I/O performance.
